mainEntity.name: How much does a Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid engine typically costs between £2,000 and £3,500 for a rebuilt unit fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from around £450 supply-only.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start-up, which may persist as the engine warms up.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2017-2020 Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid retains significant value (£5,000-£12,000 depending on condition and mileage), so a rebuilt engine at £2,000-£3,500 fitted is usually a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement typically takes 2-5 days depending on the workshop's schedule and parts availability.

mainEntity.name: What causes Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid engine failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: The K12C engine in the Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid is prone to two primary issues: timing chain tensioner wear and injector sealing problems.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the K12C and K12D engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The K12C was the original 1.2 Dualjet engine used from 2017 to 2020, producing 90hp. The K12D replaced it from 2020 onwards with 83hp and a revised 12V mild-hybrid system.

historyTimeline.h2: Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid arrived in 2017 as part of the third-generation Swift range, introducing Suzuki's K12C Dualjet engine with a 12-volt mild-hybrid system to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions without compromising the Swift's reputation for reliability and driving enjoyment.

milestones.description: K12C 1.2-litre four-cylinder Dualjet naturally aspirated petrol engine launched with 90hp, paired with a 12V mild-hybrid system (SHVS) in UK and European markets
Production continues with minor specification updates; SZ-T and SZ5 trim levels available
Facelift introduces K12D Dualjet Hybrid engine replacing K12C, with 83hp and revised mild-hybrid system
2023 - K12D continues as the sole 1.2 Dualjet Hybrid option in the UK market

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid's K12C and K12D engines are generally regarded as reliable units, but a few issues have been reported by owners. The most common concerns are timing chain tensioner wear on earlier K12C engines and injector sealing problems across the Dualjet family. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid K12C Develops Rattle
problems.rootCause: The K12C engine uses a timing chain with a hydraulic tensioner. Some owners have reported a rattling noise on cold start-up or at operating temperature, which may indicate tensioner wear or chain stretch.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain tensioner and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early with rattle; prevents further wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt K12C with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has failed or engine has other significant issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2017-2020 Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid with 40,000-70,000 miles is valued between £5,000 and £12,000 depending on condition and spec [THIRD-PARTY - Parkers/Auto Trader market observation]. With replacement cost typically under £3,500 fitted through a specialist, the investment is usually justified relative to vehicle value for most examples. However, if the vehicle has covered over 100,000 miles or shows significant other wear, weigh the replacement cost against the car's overall condition.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from your Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid on start-up, have the timing chain inspected immediately - catching it early could save you thousands. The K12C engine is generally reliable, and a timing chain tensioner replacement is a manageable repair. If the engine has already failed or is showing multiple issues, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components offers the best long-term reliability.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt K12C Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Sealing Issues - The Dualjet Weak Point on the Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid
problems.rootCause: The Dualjet engine features two injectors per cylinder. Some owners have reported injectors failing to seal properly, leading to fuel entering the cylinders after the engine is switched off.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty injectors and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early; prevents fuel dilution and catalytic converter damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with upgraded injectors, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When injector failure has caused engine damage or multiple injectors have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, a typical Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid retains sufficient value to justify either repair or replacement. For a vehicle worth £5,000-£12,000, an injector replacement at £400-£700 is excellent value if caught early. If the engine has already suffered damage, replacement is the only viable path.
problems.recommendation: If you notice a strong smell of fuel, rough running, or a check engine light on your Suzuki Swift 1.2 Dualjet Mild Hybrid, have the injectors checked immediately. The Dualjet system is sophisticated, and injector issues can lead to more serious problems if ignored. A specialist with experience on the K12C/K12D platform is recommended.
